title: Keep the business name and contact details identical across pages
statement: The trading name, street address, and telephone number are rendered from one source, so every page that shows them shows the same characters rather than variants that accumulated separately.
rationale: Contact details get copied into templates, footers, and location pages independently, and each copy then ages on its own until a visitor cannot tell which number is current.
implementation: Hold the details in one configuration record and render every appearance from it, including the footer and the structured-data node. Report divergent copies instead of picking one and rewriting the rest.

verification.method: Extract rendered name, address, and telephone strings from every route that displays them and report any route whose values differ from the configured record.

caution: The cited documentation defines the properties that carry these details without requiring internal consistency, so the requirement to render them from one source is this registry's inference and the record is tier B. Which variant is correct is a business fact, so divergence is reported rather than resolved.

title: Publish a distinct page per staffed location
statement: Each place a customer can visit has one page describing that place, with its own address, hours, contact route, and directions, rather than a shared page listing several places.
rationale: A visitor looking for one branch needs that branch's details on one page, and a combined page forces them to work out which set of details applies to the place they intend to go.
implementation: Create the page only for places that genuinely exist and are staffed, and give it content specific to that place. Do not generate a page per postcode or per service area.

verification.method: Enumerate location routes and confirm each corresponds to one real place, carrying details that differ from every other location route.

caution: The cited documentation describes marking up a location without requiring one page per location, so this record is tier B. It stops short of recommending pages for unstaffed areas, which the separate record on generated location pages treats as a defect.

title: Publish opening hours the business actually keeps
statement: Stated hours match when the door is open, including the exceptions for holidays and seasonal changes, and no hours are published for a location whose real schedule is unrecorded.
rationale: Someone travels to a place on the strength of published hours, so an hours table that is merely plausible sends people to a closed door.
implementation: Render hours from a record the location's own staff maintain, and represent exceptions explicitly rather than leaving the regular schedule to imply them. Where no record exists, omit the hours and say to contact the location.

verification.method: Compare rendered and marked-up hours for each location against the schedule record, and confirm holiday exceptions for the current period are represented.

caution: Hours are a real-world fact about a physical place that no code can observe, so this record never writes or infers them. Publishing invented hours has a direct cost to the person who travelled.

title: Describe the service area only where the business operates
statement: A declared service area covers places the business will actually travel to or serve, and is not expanded to neighbouring regions the business has no presence in or intention of reaching.
rationale: An inflated service area produces enquiries the business declines, which wastes the enquirer's time and teaches them the listing cannot be trusted.
implementation: Take the area from what operations will commit to serving and represent it once, as an area rather than as a list of separate places each implying a location. Report an unspecified area as unspecified.

verification.method: Compare declared service areas against the operational coverage record and report declared places outside it.

caution: The documentation provides the property for expressing an area but cannot say what area is true for a given business, so the boundary always comes from the business and is never widened here.

title: Relate each location node to its parent organization
statement: A location's structured-data node names the organization it belongs to, and that organization resolves to the site-level node rather than being repeated as an unrelated object on each location page.
rationale: Without the relation each location reads as an independent business, so a graph describing one company with several branches describes several companies instead.
implementation: Reference the organization by its stable identifier from every location node instead of restating the organization's properties, so one edit to the organization reaches every branch.

verification.method: Parse location nodes and confirm each names a parent organization whose identifier resolves to the site-level node.

title: Detect thin location pages generated from a template
statement: Routes produced by substituting a place name into a shared template, with no content specific to that place, are reported as a defect rather than as coverage, and no such route is generated by this process.
rationale: Pages differing only by a place name exist to catch queries rather than to serve the person who arrives, which is the pattern search platforms document as disallowed.
implementation: Compare location routes against each other and report clusters whose text is identical apart from substituted place names. Consolidate them into the pages that describe real places, and never expand the set.

verification.method: Extract body text from every location route, measure pairwise similarity after removing place names, and report clusters above the reporting threshold.

caution: The cited policy describes this pattern as disallowed, so generating such pages is out of scope for this process under any instruction. Consolidating existing ones removes published addresses, which is why the change is not automatic.
